title: Silk Road
subject: English

notes.heading: Theme
notes.text: The travelogue describes the intense challenges, geographical harshness, and physical resilience involved in high-altitude pilgrimages, while highlighting the rewarding nature of cross-cultural human companionship.

summary: "Silk Road" by Nick Middleton is a gripping travelogue that narrates the author's arduous journey from the slopes of Ravu to the sacred Mount Kailash to complete the Buddhist pilgrimage known as the Kora. The journey begins with a heartfelt farewell at Ravu, where a local woman named Lhamo gifts the author a long-sleeved sheepskin coat to protect him against the biting high-altitude cold. Accompanying him are Tsetan, an expert local driver and guide, and Daniel, a companion who travels with them until the town of Hor. As they navigate the ancient Silk Road route, they encounter a landscape dominated by vast plains, rolling hills, solitary drokbas (nomadic shepherds) tending their flocks, and aggressive Tibetan mastiffs that ferociously guard the nomad tents. As the vehicle climbs higher, the author suffers from a severe headache caused by the sudden drop in atmospheric pressure and rapidly thinning oxygen. After Daniel departs at Hor—a dreary, dust-choked town on the shore of Lake Manasarovar—the author’s health deteriorates further. Upon reaching Darchen, he suffers from a acute sinus blockage that prevents him from sleeping, forcing a concerned Tsetan to take him to the Darchen Medical College. A Tibetan doctor prescribes a five-day course of traditional herbal medicines that successfully cures his respiratory issues. Though his health returns, the author faces a new setback when he realizes he has arrived too early in the pilgrimage season; the town of Darchen is nearly deserted, and there are no other pilgrims with whom he can undertake the challenging trek. This loneliness and frustration vanish when he meets Norbu, an English-speaking Tibetan academic working at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences in Beijing, who has also come to write an essay on the Kora. Since Norbu is also unaccustomed to heavy physical exertion and prefers a companion, the author realizes they make a perfect team. Tsetan departs for Lhasa, leaving the duo to embark on their shared pilgrimage, demonstrating that determination and unexpected companionship can help overcome the harshest physical and geographical barriers.

qa.q: Give reasons why the article has been titled ‘Silk Road’.
qa.a: The chapter is titled Silk Road because the narrator travels through the ancient trade route connecting Tibet with other parts of Asia. His journey follows a route historically used for trading silk and other goods.

qa.q: Give reasons why the author’s experience of Lake Manasarovar was unforgettable.
qa.a: The author found Lake Manasarovar unforgettable because of its beautiful surroundings, clear blue water and religious importance. The peaceful atmosphere and the magnificent landscape made a deep impression on him.

qa.q: Give reasons why Tsetan was a good guide.
qa.a: Tsetan was a good guide because he was experienced, careful and familiar with the difficult mountain roads. He drove safely through dangerous areas and helped the author during the journey.

qa.q: Briefly describe the narrator’s journey from Ravu to Darchen.
qa.a: The narrator travelled from Ravu towards Darchen with Tsetan and Daniel. They crossed high mountain passes and difficult roads while facing cold weather and thin air. After reaching Hor, they travelled along the banks of Lake Manasarovar and finally reached Darchen, where the narrator rested and prepared for the next part of his journey.

qa.q: Describe the difficulties faced by the narrator on his journey.
qa.a: The narrator faced several difficulties because of the high altitude and harsh weather. He suffered from breathlessness, headache and weakness due to the lack of oxygen. The roads were rough and dangerous, and the cold was severe. Despite these difficulties, he continued his journey.

qa.q: The chapter has many descriptions of nature. Give examples.
qa.a: The chapter contains vivid descriptions of the Tibetan landscape. The narrator describes the snow-covered mountains, vast plains, beautiful Lake Manasarovar and the cold, dry surroundings. These descriptions show the beauty and harshness of the natural environment.

qa.q: Explain the title “Silk Road” in the context of the chapter.
qa.a: The title refers to the ancient Silk Road, a network of trade routes connecting different parts of Asia. The narrator travels through a part of this historic route in Tibet. The journey allows him to experience the landscape, culture and life of the people living along the route.
